nodes.prompt: QA validation only for issue 08. Verify that the real constellation supports agent questions, answers, inactive suggestions, saved node movement and reopening. Test answers and acceptance in this map are fixtures, not user product decisions.
nodes.body:
Observed in the live browser: the QA answer returned the root to Queued. The public CLI then claimed the same root with that answer in its context. Dragging Verify saved positions stored x=104.34782608695654 and y=-219.37391304347824. After reloading, the node had those exact coordinates and its SVG connection ended at the same point. Both suggested branches remained Unexplored. Dark mode also survived the reload.

This is a real Codex validation result based on local code, automated checks, CLI responses, and browser observations. The answer itself is explicitly a QA fixture. It is not a user product decision.

Further trial work: explicitly activate a suggested branch, check cancel/retry and acceptance presentation, then return to the owner's original map.

nodes.title: Verify saved positions
nodes.prompt: Move this node, reload the page, and confirm the saved coordinates and incident connections are restored.
nodes.body:
The browser moved this node to x=104.34782608695654, y=-219.37391304347824; reloading restored it and its incident edge. Alt+Right then saved x=128.34782608695656 with the same y while this job was running. The canonical JSON reached revision 13.

The explicit activation/cancel/retry UI sequence was Queued, Ready to retry, Queued. The CLI claimed only the retried branch; Review dense maps later remained suggested. These are validation observations in a QA map, not owner product decisions.

The following possible direction remains unactivated. Dense real-world navigation is outside this small end-to-end trial.

The static layout preserves explicit coordinates and keeps suggested nodes inactive. Automated HTTP coverage confirms that moving a claimed node does not invalidate its research and that coordinates survive a server restart. The browser still needs to exercise movement and reopening.
